title: 12 Marketing Ideas for Barber Shops That Actually Fill Chairs (2026)

facts.fact: The page was last updated on May 26, 2026.
facts.quote: Last updated May 26, 2026 · By Rob P., Strategy

facts.fact: The vendor estimates that a client on a standing three-week schedule is worth roughly 17 cuts a year, versus roughly 8 for a client who rebooks whenever they remember.
facts.quote: A client on a standing three-week schedule is roughly 17 cuts a year; the same client rebooking whenever they remember might be 8.

facts.fact: The vendor's example referral card offers $5 off for the referring client and $5 off for the new client.
facts.quote: '$5 off for you, $5 off for them.'

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a Facebook or Instagram ad radius of 3 to 5 miles for a barbershop.
facts.quote: 3–5 miles. People don't drive across town for a fade.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends barbershop before-and-after social videos of 15 to 30 seconds, shot vertically.
facts.quote: Fifteen to thirty seconds. Vertical. No production required.

facts.fact: The vendor advises sending one friendly message to any client who hasn't visited in six weeks.
facts.quote: Anyone who hasn't been in for six weeks gets one friendly message.

facts.fact: When someone searches 'barber near me,' Google's map shows three businesses in the local pack.
facts.quote: When someone searches 'barber near me,' Google shows a map with three businesses.

facts.fact: The vendor advises filming one session and posting the same clip to three short-video platforms: TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
facts.quote: Post the same clip to TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. One filming session, three platforms.
